text:
`python3 -m unittest` now reports all 25 tests passing. I changed six places in `taskflow/`:

- **`queue.py`:** `_Entry.sort_key` returned `(seq, -priority)`. It now returns `(-priority, seq)`, so higher priority pops first and ties go in insertion order.
- **`retry.py`:** `should_retry` used `attempts_made < max_attempts - 1`, which gave up one attempt early. It now uses `attempts_made < max_attempts`.
- **`resources.py`:** `ResourcePool.release` did `used -= 1` instead of `used -= cost`, which leaked capacity.
- **`events.py`:** `_prefix_matches` had its arguments reversed (`prefix.startswith(topic + ".")`). It now checks `topic.startswith(prefix + ".")`.
- **`statemachine.py`:** `batch_order_ok` had its comparison backwards. Priorities within an admission batch must be non-increasing, so it now checks `current <= prev`.
- **`config.py`:** `deep_merge` recursed with its arguments swapped, so defaults overrode the task's own values. It now merges `(result[key], value)`.
- **`scheduler.py`:** `_cascade_skip` used `dag.dependents`, which returns only direct children. It now uses `dag.transitive_dependents`, so everything downstream of a permanent failure is skipped.

I didn't modify any tests.
